reported.title: pH conversion returns millivolts instead of pH
reported.description: computePh() at lines 21-24 simply returns the millivolt value unchanged, so the required division by 500 mV/pH is never performed. The measured output confirms this: at 9.01 s the firmware printed 4491.69 pH while the injected value was 8.68-9.02 pH, off by 4482.7 pH, and every scenario shows printed values in the hundreds/thousands (e.g. 493.65 pH, 1001.96 pH, 5000 pH). Firmware printed 4491.69 pH at 9.01 s while the injected input was 8.68 to 9.02 pH: off by 4482.7 pH (tolerance ±0.2). 9 of 9 values were wrong.

reported.title: Alert LED driven from unscaled millivolt value
reported.description: The alert comparison at line 66 tests lastPh, which is actually millivolts because computePh() (lines 21-24) never divides by 500. Since millivolts are almost always far above 7.20, D13 is driven LOW when it should be HIGH; measured evidence shows D13 not HIGH for 1270 ms at 500 ms in the nominal ramp and 1284 ms in the out-of-range scenario. D13 was in the wrong state for 4850 ms across 6 interval(s), first at 500 ms: D13 was not HIGH for 500 ms while required (grace 500 ms).

judge_input.spec:
- Linearized pH probe on A0 with scale 500 mV/pH (0 mV → pH 0.0); low-pH alert LED on D13.
- Convert ADC samples using a 5.000 V / 1023 full-scale span, then divide millivolts by 500 to obtain pH.
- Print exactly one line every 1000 ms matching `pH: <value>` with two decimal places.
- Printed pH must stay within ±0.20 of the injected probe value.
- Drive D13 HIGH when reported pH is below 7.20; otherwise drive D13 LOW.
- Keep logging while the alert LED is on or off.
